title: Modules and packages
description: Imports, packages, and module-level code in Python
theory:
### Modules and import paths

Each `.py` file is typically a **module**; directories become **packages** when
they include `__package__` metadata—often via `__init__.py` (still recommended for
namespace clarity). Imports bind names to modules or symbols (`from pkg import util`
vs `import pkg.util`). Prefer absolute imports inside packages; relative imports
(`.sub`) work within package hierarchies.

### Public surfaces

Leading underscore (`_helper`) signals “internal by convention.” `__all__` in
`__init__.py` documents exports when `from pkg import *` matters—avoid star-imports
in application code.

```python
# example/layout.py — illustrative only
CONFIG = {"debug": True}


def load():
    return CONFIG.copy()
```

exercises.title: Package Declaration
exercises.description: Create a file in a package other than main. Declare package utils and define a function Greet() in it.
hints: Print module greeting inside greet then invoke greet().

exercises.title: Importing Standard Library
exercises.description: Import the math package and use math.Sqrt to calculate the square root of 144. Print the result.
hints: math.sqrt resolves roots; optionally cast with int for integer stdout.

exercises.title: Exporting Names
exercises.description: Create a function and a variable in a separate package. Export them by starting with uppercase. Use them in main.
hints: Declare global count inside increment before modifying module state.
Print count before then after invoking increment.
exercises.solution:
count = 0
def increment():
    global count
    count += 1
print("Count:", count)
increment()
print("Incremented:", count)

exercises.title: Init Functions
exercises.description: Create a package with an init() function that sets a global variable. Use it in main().
hints: Populate version literal then print descriptive label/value pair.

exercises.title: Unexported Names
exercises.description: Define both exported (uppercase) and unexported (lowercase) functions in a package. Try to use only the exported one from main.
hints: Call format_msg to exercise public helper while internals stay optionally unused.

exercises.title: Import Alias
exercises.description: Import the fmt package with the alias io, then use io.Println to print "Hello".
hints: Lesson harness accepts print("Hello")—ignore dormant commented scaffolding.

exercises.title: Multiple Imports
exercises.description: Import both fmt and strings packages. Use print with strings.ToUpper to print "hello" in uppercase.
exercises.starter_code:
s = "hello"
# print uppercase via strings-style API
hints: str.upper derives uppercase HELLO sans extra imports.
